brief: Every tool call the model proposes passes through the gateway before anything happens. The gateway has four stages, and the order they run in decides what can go wrong.
The pipeline below starts in a deliberately wrong order. Validation runs first and leaks the schema to callers who should be denied, and the raw tool output is never typed.
Send six calls to the refund_order tool and watch what each stage does. Then reorder the stages until every call returns its expected typed result with no hazards.

stages.label: Authorise
stages.description: Check the calling principal against the tool's allowlist and stop with DENIED if it is not listed.

stages.label: Validate
stages.description: Check the arguments against the tool's schema and stop with INVALID if they do not match.

stages.label: Execute
stages.description: Run the tool under the caller's identity and cut it off when the per-call timeout expires.

stages.label: Type the result
stages.description: Map the raw outcome to SUCCESS, EMPTY or UNAVAILABLE so the orchestrator knows who acts next.

tool.name: refund_order
tool.description: Refunds part or all of one paid order to the original payment method. Use only when a support case confirms a refund is due. Not for order lookups or cancellations.
tool.argsSchema: { order_id: string (required), amount: number > 0 (required), reason: one of damaged | late | not_received | duplicate_charge }

calls.title: Valid refund by a support agent
Unlisted bot probes with bad arguments
Unlisted bot sends a well-formed refund
Support agent sends a negative amount

challenge.instruction: Reorder the four stages so that all six calls return their expected typed result with zero hazards.
